recommended_fix: Replace full name as one unit; verify no surname substring overlap with source.

recommended_fix: Treat address/city/county/ZIP as one geography set; verify all four change together.

why_issue: Real email retained verbatim; also inconsistent with the new fake name 'Carmen L. Delgado' used elsewhere in the same document.

original_value: Race: Hispanic or Latino / Ethnicity: Mexican / Occupation: Elementary School Teacher
output_value: Race: White / Ethnicity: German / Occupation: Accountant
why_issue: These are non-identifying demographic fields per policy and should be preserved unchanged, not swapped for different values.
recommended_fix: Tighten field rules to explicitly preserve race/ethnicity/occupation; only replace fields on the identifier list.

original_value: Patient: Harold Finch (header); 'Mr. Finch' in body text
output_value: Patient: Gerald Foster (header, correctly changed); body still says 'Mr. Finch'
why_issue: Structured Patient field was de-identified but the real surname leaked in the free-text body, contradicting the header name.
recommended_fix: Run a name-consistency pass across the full document body, not just structured fields; verify no source-name substrings remain anywhere in the text.

original_value: DIAGNOSIS: Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
why_issue: Diagnosis is protected clinical content per policy and should be preserved unchanged; it was replaced with an unrelated condition, which could mislead downstream clinical use.
recommended_fix: Whitelist clinical fields (diagnosis, meds, vitals, device model, blood type) and diff-check them for byte-identical output.

original_value: Nationality: Nigerian/Nigeria; Religion: Baptist; Occupation: Retired Electrical Engineer; Height/Weight: 5 ft 10 in/182 lbs; Blood Type: O positive; Astrological Sign: Capricorn
output_value: Nationality: Brazilian/Brazil; Religion: Catholic; Occupation: Retired Accountant; Height/Weight: 5 ft 8 in/168 lbs; Blood Type: AB negative; Astrological Sign: Aquarius
why_issue: None of these fields are identifiers per policy - they are non-identifying demographic/clinical fields that should be preserved unchanged. Nearly the entire questionnaire was altered with no policy basis. Blood type change is especially concerning since it is medically significant (O positive vs AB negative) and explicitly named in the preserve list.
recommended_fix: Tighten field-level rules to clearly separate replace categories (name, date, contact, ID, geography) from preserve categories (demographics, vitals, blood type, diagnosis, meds); block substitution entirely for preserve-category fields.
notes: Age, marital status, and education level were correctly left unchanged in this same document - shows the model can preserve fields correctly, just inconsistently.

why_issue: URL token left completely unreplaced. It encodes the real patient initials (LF for Lydia Fairbanks) and the real appointment date (20250328), fully re-identifying her even though the PATIENT and EMAIL fields were correctly changed to Diane Hayes elsewhere in the same document.
recommended_fix: Regenerate all URL and token fields from the surrogate identity, not the source; block any derived token built from real initials or dates.
notes: Non-revealing violation and leak in one field; shows model can de-identify structured fields but miss derived technical fields like URL slugs.

why_issue: Real IP address passed through with no substitution.
recommended_fix: Add IP address to the identifier detection pattern set; require every IP field to differ from the source value.

why_issue: Real surname retained while only the first name changed; same partial-name-leak pattern seen in doc_01.
recommended_fix: Replace full name as one unit; verify no surname substring overlap with source.

why_issue: Email and callback number leaked verbatim and are inconsistent with the new fake patient name (Janet Patel); portal token SP-4492 also encodes the real patient initials (Sunita Patel), a non-revealing violation. IP address in the same entry was correctly replaced, so the model appears to reliably miss email, URL tokens, and phone numbers in this message-log format specifically.
recommended_fix: Add email, URL-token, and phone detection to the same identifier pass already working for IP addresses in this format.

why_issue: Staff member's first name retained while surname changed; mirror image of the patient partial-name leak, lower severity since it identifies staff rather than the patient.
recommended_fix: Apply the same full-name-as-one-unit replacement rule to all person names in the document, not only the patient.

why_issue: Interval between linked dates changed, violating the requirement that date relationships be preserved.
recommended_fix: Shift all dates within a document by one consistent random offset rather than randomizing each date independently.

output_value: Brenda Dubois - but body still reads Mr. Dubois and his car
why_issue: Patient renamed to a female-reading name but honorific and pronouns in the body were not updated to match, creating an internal contradiction.
recommended_fix: Update gendered honorifics and pronouns as part of the name-substitution step rather than independently.

output_value: 1FTFW1E8 (8 characters - exact first 8 characters of the real VIN)
why_issue: Fake VIN is a truncated copy of the real VIN, both a partial leak and the wrong length since real VINs are always 17 characters.
recommended_fix: Generate fully synthetic 17-character VINs; reject any output sharing a run of more than 4 characters with the source VIN.

why_issue: Vehicle make/model is explicitly listed as preserve-content, not an identifier, but was changed to a different vehicle.
recommended_fix: Whitelist vehicle make/model alongside diagnosis, blood type, and device model for byte-identical preservation.

why_issue: Real driver's license number retained verbatim; explicitly required to be replaced.
recommended_fix: Add driver's license numbers to the same identifier detection pass as SSN/MRN/account numbers.

why_issue: Real county retained even though street address and city were both correctly replaced.
recommended_fix: Treat address/city/county/ZIP as one geography set and verify all components change together, same pattern seen in doc_01.

why_issue: Device model name is explicitly listed as preserve-content, not an identifier, but was changed to a different manufacturer and model.
recommended_fix: Whitelist device model name alongside diagnosis, blood type, and vehicle make/model for byte-identical preservation.

why_issue: Real device serial number retained verbatim. Its prefix (BSC-X4) denotes the original Boston Scientific device, which now contradicts the output's altered device model (Medtronic Claria), stacking a leak on top of an internal inconsistency.
recommended_fix: Add device serial numbers to the same identifier detection pass as SSN/MRN/DL/account numbers.

why_issue: Real account number retained verbatim; explicitly required to be replaced.
recommended_fix: Add exact-match check flagging output as a defect whenever an identifier field equals its source value.

why_issue: Fake fax number has an extra digit appended, making it an invalid phone/fax format.
recommended_fix: Add regex format validators per field type (phone, fax, SSN, VIN, DL) as a post-generation QA gate.

why_issue: Real ZIP and county retained even though city was correctly replaced; same incomplete-geography-set pattern seen in doc_01 and doc_06.
recommended_fix: Treat address/city/county/ZIP as one geography set and verify all four components change together.

original_value: Rosa M. Delgado, MRN 7734821, SSN 284-56-7901 (same real patient appears in doc_01 and doc_08)
output_value: Carmen L. Delgado (doc_01 output) vs. Brenda Caldwell (doc_08 output)
why_issue: The same real patient, confirmed via matching real MRN and SSN in both original documents, was mapped to two different fake identities across the two documents, breaking cross-document consistency.
recommended_fix: Maintain a persistent per-patient entity-to-surrogate map keyed on stable real identifiers (MRN/SSN), reused across all documents referencing that patient.
notes: Core cross-document consistency failure explicitly called out in the policy as a requirement.
